structuralDecisions.decision: Add a second boolean, MustNotExist, to state.PathClaim (internal/state/claims.go) rather than replacing MustExist with a tri-state enum (Exists/Deleted/Unchecked).
structuralDecisions.rationale: The existing MustExist doc comment already anticipates this exact extension ("the flag exists so a future field can opt out explicitly"). Every PathClaims() implementation sets exactly one claim kind per field literal — there is no call site today, nor any planned one, that needs 'neither' or 'both' as a real state. A two-boolean struct is the smaller diff: orchestrator's verifyOneClaim dispatches on two conditions it already partially has, instead of introducing a new named type that every existing claim literal (filesCreated, filesModified, testFilesCreated, testFilesModified, security's filesModified) would need to be rewritten to use.
tradeOffs: The shape is nominally capable of representing an invalid state (MustExist: true, MustNotExist: true) that an enum could not express. This is accepted because nothing constructs a claim that way, and the fitness function below gives it a test-level guard instead of a type-level one.

A third claim kind in the future (e.g. 'must exist AND have changed, full stop, no posture leniency') would need a third boolean rather than a third enum value — acceptable now, revisit if a third kind actually arrives.

fitness.property: Every PathClaim literal returned by ImplementationState.PathClaims(), QAState.PathClaims(), and SecurityState.PathClaims() sets exactly one of MustExist or MustNotExist to true, never both and never neither.
fitness.verification: internal/orchestrator/claims_test.go table test covering each PathClaims() implementation's output; go vet / code review as a secondary check since this is a value-level invariant, not a type-level one

structuralDecisions.decision: Split verifyOneClaim (internal/orchestrator/claims.go) into a small dispatcher plus two bodies: verifyExistenceClaim (the current MustExist body, renamed, unchanged behavior and wording) and a new verifyDeletionClaim for MustNotExist.
structuralDecisions.rationale: verifyOneClaim's body already checks !claim.MustExist and returns nil; adding the deletion branch inline would push a single function across two independent failure modes (existence-required vs absence-required) and risk exceeding the complexity-7 budget design-principles.md and CLAUDE.md both set. Naming the split keeps each function doing one thing, which is also what the Fowler-operations habit this architecture process uses calls for: this is Extract Function, applied because the existing function's reason to change is about to become two reasons.
tradeOffs: One more function and one more name to keep in sync with the dispatcher, for a net gain in testability — each body gets its own table-test rows instead of one function's test covering two unrelated behaviors.

fitness.property: Cyclomatic complexity < 7 on verifyOneClaim's dispatcher, verifyExistenceClaim, and verifyDeletionClaim individually
fitness.verification: golangci-lint run (gocyclo, min-complexity: 7 — already enabled in .golangci.yml)

structuralDecisions.decision: verifyDeletionClaim's two failure modes have different data requirements: the "still exists" check is a pure filesystem stat and always runs; the "no such file was there to delete" check requires git history and MUST run only when changed != nil (i.e. the WorkTree answered successfully this run) — not merely when len(changed) == 0.
structuralDecisions.rationale: changedPaths() (internal/orchestrator/posture.go:110) returns nil for both 'posture checking disabled' (no WorkTree) and 'ChangedPaths() errored', and returns a non-nil map — possibly empty — when git ran and genuinely found nothing uncommitted. Those are different facts: a nil map means this executor has no opinion about history; a non-nil empty map means git looked and the claimed path was not among the changes, which is real evidence a fabricated deletion claim should be caught by. Checking len(changed)==0 (the pattern warnUntouched already uses, two functions up in the same file) would silently skip the 'no such file was there to delete' failure in the empty-but-observed case, which is exactly the fabrication case AC #4 exists to catch. Pin the check to the nil/non-nil distinction the executor's own doc comment on changedPaths() already promises, not emptiness.
tradeOffs: This only catches a never-existed path when posture checking is configured (a WorkTree is wired in). With no WorkTree, a stage can claim a deletion for a path that was never there and the claim passes — the same limitation every other posture-dependent check in this file already has, and consistent with 'nothing is auto-approved and this check is advisory where the tree can't be observed' rather than a new gap this feature introduces.

Depends on the pipeline's existing assumption (shared/rules/approval-gates.md gate #2) that a stage does not commit its own work mid-run — git-commit is a human-gated action, so HEAD stays fixed for the duration of a stage and git status --porcelain output is equivalent to 'changed since this stage's base commit'. If that assumption is ever relaxed, this check and the rest of posture checking break together, not just this feature.

fitness.property: A filesDeleted/testFilesDeleted claim for a path absent from disk and absent from a non-nil changed set fails with the exact 'no such file was there to delete' wording; the same claim with a nil changed set (no WorkTree) does not fail on that specific check
fitness.verification: internal/orchestrator/claims_test.go: table rows for (a) real deletion with WorkTree configured — passes, (b) claimed-but-still-exists — fails 'still exists' regardless of WorkTree, (c) never-existed path with WorkTree configured and empty ChangedPaths() — fails 'no such file was there to delete', (d) never-existed path with no WorkTree (nil changed) — does not fail on this check

structuralDecisions.decision: No new WorkTree method. internal/worktree/git.go's existing ChangedPaths() (git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all) already reports a deleted tracked file by its own path, and a git-detected rename as 'old -> new' split into both halves by the existing splitRename helper — confirmed by reading the implementation, not assumed.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Extending the WorkTree interface would require changing internal/worktree/git.go and every test fake implementing it (internal/orchestrator/post_review_test.go's editingTree, internal/orchestrator/posture_test.go's changingTree, internal/factory/faults_test.go's faultyTree) — all outside scope.paths (internal/state/**, internal/orchestrator/**, shared/schemas/pipeline/**, docs/features/state-files-deleted/**). The data this feature needs is already surfaced by the method that exists.
tradeOffs: verifyDeletionClaim reads the same map shape (map[string]bool keyed by slash-separated repo-relative path) the existence-claim path already consumes, rather than a purpose-built 'what was deleted' signal — acceptable since porcelain output already resolves to exactly the set of changed paths this check needs, deletions included.

structuralDecisions.decision: requireNoRenameArrows(claims []state.PathClaim) error lives once in internal/state/claims.go and is called from ImplementationState.Validate(), QAState.Validate(), and SecurityState.Validate() via each type's own PathClaims() — not duplicated three times.
structuralDecisions.rationale: design-principles.md's Simple Design priority #3 (no duplication) and the Boy Scout Rule both apply directly: PathClaims() already exists as the one place each type declares its path-naming fields together, so the rename-arrow check reads that same list instead of re-enumerating fields per type.
tradeOffs: Couples the three Validate() methods to one shared helper's exact error wording — acceptable since the acceptance criteria require one consistent message across all three types.

antiPatternChecks.notes: The change touches ~10 files, which looks like shotgun surgery on its face, but every touch is a narrow, mechanical propagation of one additive field through an already-established seam (struct field -> PathClaims() entry -> claims.go verifier -> render section -> generated schema -> tests). The seam existed before this feature (filesCreated/filesModified already flow through the same files); this is the seam working as designed, not fragile coupling.

refactoringOpportunities.target: internal/orchestrator/claims.go warnUntouched (existing, pre-dates this feature) vs the new verifyDeletionClaim
refactoringOpportunities.reason: warnUntouched treats 'posture checking configured' as len(changed) == 0 (empty means not-observed), while verifyDeletionClaim (this feature) treats it as changed != nil (nil means not-observed, a non-nil empty map is real evidence). Both are individually correct for their own risk profile — warnUntouched is a soft warning where under-firing is safe, verifyDeletionClaim is a hard gate where it isn't — but the inconsistency is worth a dedicated harmonization pass later. Do not fix now: test-repair-contract.md and this codebase's own convention keep refactoring and behavior changes in separate commits, and warnUntouched has no test coverage gap this feature is responsible for closing.

developerHandoffNotes: Dispatch on claim.MustExist vs claim.MustNotExist in a small top-level function; keep the renamed verifyExistenceClaim's behavior and wording byte-for-byte identical to today's verifyOneClaim MustExist branch.

verifyDeletionClaim's 'still exists' failure is unconditional (pure filesystem stat); its 'no such file was there to delete' failure must check changed != nil, not len(changed) == 0 — see the structural decision above for why the distinction matters here specifically.

SecurityState currently has no dedicated test file — its tests live in internal/state/implementation_chain_test.go. Add the rename-arrow rejection case for SecurityState.FilesModified there, not in a new file, unless the test file is reorganized as a separate task.

Do not touch internal/worktree/git.go or any WorkTree test fake (editingTree, changingTree, faultyTree) — ChangedPaths() already surfaces both a deleted tracked file (its own path) and a detected rename (both halves, via splitRename) with no interface change needed.

requireNoRenameArrows must be called from all three Validate() methods (ImplementationState, QAState, SecurityState) via each type's own PathClaims() — one function, three call sites, not three copies of the substring check.

No new telemetry or signal is introduced — the existing ClaimError struct carries the new 'still exists' / 'no such file was there to delete' Problem strings exactly as it already carries today's wording; nothing in architecture-guardrails.md #8/#9 is newly implicated.
